sheets.name: Read_me
rows: RIVERKNOLL RENEWAL | MATERIAL LIST BY AREA (v1, Nov 26 2026)

For proofing. Ties to feasibility model v24: the whole building is System 3E perlite blocks (outside walls, party walls, partitions), plastered inside and rendered outside, with a concrete plank second floor. No wood framing, sheathing, house wrap or stud insulation; only the roof trusses are wood. Local suppliers are on Local_Suppliers.
- Townhome_4bed: one interior 4-bed townhome, 25 x 32 ft, two floors, 1,600 SF, by area.
- Accessible_End_Unit: one single-level accessible end unit, 2 beds, 920 SF.
- Row_of_10: 8 townhomes + 2 end units, plus what the row changes (side walls, party walls).
- Check_vs_Model: how the list compares with model v24's $305/SF and why there is a gap.
- Inputs: dimensions and counts. Change a yellow cell and every list updates.
- Sources: every unit cost source with its link.
Colour key: yellow quantity = assumed by me, check it. Orange unit cost = estimate with no source yet, check it with a quote.
Low / Mid / High: the low and high ends of each sourced range; Mid is the midpoint unless the note says otherwise.
Unit costs are installed prices (material plus trade labor), national, 2025-26. They are not Rochester bids.

Counts: The organizer's old-unit counts (4 windows, 2 exterior doors, 5 interior doors, 1 double closet) are kept, plus what a new 4-bed needs (8 interior doors, 4 closets, 4 more windows for bedroom egress).
Cost per SF in model v24: building $305/SF (two-story row), all in $595/SF; three-story row $294 and $573. (Model v22 was $274 and $536, before System 3E was priced as blocks.)

rows: HOW THE LIST TIES TO MODEL v24 ($305/SF building cost, whole building in System 3E)
This list, with contractor overhead and profit (mid)
Model v24 building cost per SF (two-story row)
Model v24 building cost per townhome (1,626.67 SF average)
Model v24 cost scaled to 1,600 SF
Gap per townhome (model minus list, mid)
List as a share of the model
Benchmark: NAHB 2024 average construction cost per SF (S24)
Benchmark: ICC R-3 type VB per SF, national, Feb 2026 (S25)
Model v24 all-in per SF (adds site, design, contingency, inflation, financing)
1. The cost guides are national homeowner prices for single trades. A Rochester bid from a commercial general contractor would run higher.
2. NY prevailing wage could apply if public money pays 30% or more of a project over $5M (NY Labor Law 224-a). That would raise labor cost a lot. A lawyer should confirm whether it applies here.

3. Model v22 set its $300/SF base from student housing projects and benchmarks (APX, SUNY cost per bed, the Lodge and Apex). Those include institutional durability specs, commercial contracting and project management that a townhome cost guide leaves out.

4. Not in the list: permits, temporary power and heat, winter conditions, dumpsters, cleaning, insurance and bonds, testing, punch list. Site work, design, contingency, inflation and financing are already separate in the model.

5. What it means: this list comes to about $164/SF at mid with contractor overhead and profit ($98 low, $260 high), close to the national benchmarks of $162 (NAHB) and $176 (ICC). The model's $305/SF (v24, whole building in System 3E) is the conservative, institutional number. Only a Rochester contractor quote can say which is right for Riverknoll, so the model keeps $305 until then.
